::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Understanding the Dihedral group, $D_n$](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/3586877/understanding-the-dihedral-group-d-n), asked by [Partey5](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/617302/partey5) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2020-03-19; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> I know what the dihedral group is, the group of symmetries (length-preserving) functions of a regular n-gon.
> However, when it is referring to the symmetries of the regular n-gon what is it referring to?
> Is it referring to the symmetries of:
> The set of vertices on the n-gon, the set of points in the n-gon or the set of points on the edges of the n-gon ?
>
> Also is it considering these points as points in the complex plane?
:::

All points of the polygon (interior and boundary) are defined by the vertices.  So a symmetry of the polygon is a permutation of the vertices.  

But not every permutation of the vertices is a symmetry of the polygon.  For instance, swapping two adjacent vertices of a square isn't a symmetry of the square.
